definitions.explanation: An introductory section at the beginning of a book or document, typically written by the author to explain the purpose, scope, or background of the work.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}の{前書|まえが}きは{著者|ちょしゃ}が{書|か}いた。
examples.english: The author wrote this book's preface.

examples.japanese: {前書|まえが}きには、この{研究|けんきゅう}の{目的|もくてき}と{背景|はいけい}が{書|か}かれている。
examples.english: The preface describes the purpose and background of this research.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {前|まえ} (before, front) + {書|か}き (writing). Refers specifically to the introductory text that precedes the main content of a book or document.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {前書|まえが}きを{書|か}く (to write a preface)
- {前書|まえが}きに{述|の}べる (to state in the preface)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {序文|じょぶん}: a more formal term for a preface or introduction, often used for academic or literary works
- {後書|あとが}き: afterword — the concluding remarks at the end of a book
